forces: The self-hosted SonarQube server is unavailable during the SonarQube Cloud migration (#963), so the sonar job fails red on every trusted pull request and main push even though it is no longer a required check.
The ci-topology requirement forbids a pass-shaped green that verified nothing, so disabled analysis must render as a skip, never as a success.
The existing job guard keeps restricted Sonar secrets away from fork and Dependabot pull requests, and that trust boundary must not weaken.
A lost or mistyped setting must not silently turn analysis off once the migration ends.

evidence_ids: Workflow-condition tests evaluate the real sonar if with SONAR_ANALYSIS set to disabled and observe a skip for a main push and a trusted PR.
Workflow-condition tests run the job for an unset variable and for values other than disabled, and replacing the switch predicate with true makes a disabled event run.
The existing fork, Dependabot-actor and Dependabot-author cases and predicate-removal mutations still pass, and the untrusted-events test still asserts static and mutation jobs stay unconditional.

security_justification.trust_boundary: Fork and Dependabot PRs still skip private Sonar analysis through the unchanged predicates; the new switch can only remove analysis, never extend it to an untrusted event.
security_justification.authority_provenance: The switch reads a repository variable that only repository administrators can set. Actor, author and head-repository trust still come from GitHub event metadata.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: No token is created, copied or exposed. Sonar authentication, secrets and the quality gate are unchanged when analysis runs.
security_justification.audit_integrity: GitHub records a skipped job distinctly from a successful one, so disabled analysis never appears as a pass. Frozen contract events and generated artifacts are unchanged.
security_justification.confidentiality: Skipping the job only reduces where Sonar secrets are present. Tests use synthetic public event identities and no credentials.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Only the workflow, its trust-boundary regression test and this change's planning artifacts are owned. Repository settings changes happen under #963, outside this diff.
security_justification.fail_posture: An unset or mistyped variable runs the analysis. Only the exact value disabled skips it, and scan or quality-gate failures still fail whenever the job runs.
security_justification.error_disclosure: The condition and tests handle public repository, login and variable metadata. No new credential or payload diagnostic is emitted.
security_justification.concurrency: No worker, shared state or CI concurrency setting changes. The job's dependency on coverage and its scan ordering remain.
security_justification.lifecycle: The assessment precedes the implementation in submitted history. The restore order (delete the variable, observe a green run, then re-require the context) is recorded on #963; archive is a separate step.
security_justification.resource_retention: A skipped job allocates no Sonar runner, cache or artifact. Trusted caches, artifacts and retention are unchanged.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: The scan retry and coverage-download retry are unchanged when the job runs; a skipped job executes neither.
security_justification.cryptography: No signing, hashing, verification algorithm or secret-storage policy changes.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: No personal payload, telemetry, event transformation or privacy policy changes. Fixtures use synthetic event metadata.
security_justification.external_security_integration: No analysis service, collector or integration is added. The existing Sonar integration can be paused, and only by the repository owner.
